title: Install Forgel Code with one command via an installer script
requirements: R1: `install.sh` exists at the repository root with the executable bit set and is valid POSIX `sh` (runs under `sh`, not only `bash`).

R2: `install.sh` depends only on `sh` standard utilities and Python 3; it does not require a pre-existing virtualenv, network access when given a local source, or any package manager other than the Python tool it detects.
R3: `install.sh` installs the client into `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` when set, otherwise `$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code`; installing must not require virtualenv activation.
R4: `install.sh` writes an executable `forgel-code` launcher into `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` when set, otherwise `$HOME/.local/bin`; running that launcher without activation must work.

R5: `install.sh` adds the bin directory to PATH exactly once, inside a block delimited by a clearly marked start and end comment, in the shell profile selected from `$SHELL` (falling back to `$HOME/.profile`); no second block is appended on re-run.
R6: When the opt-out environment variable is set, `install.sh` opens no profile file for writing and instead prints exactly the `export PATH=...` line the user must add.
R7: On success `install.sh` prints the installed version and exits with status 0.
R8: Re-running `install.sh` over an existing installation replaces the installation, leaves exactly one PATH block, and exits with status 0.
R9: `install.sh --uninstall` removes the installation directory, the `forgel-code` launcher, and the marked PATH block that the installer added, and exits with status 0.
R10: `install.sh` accepts a local source tree (offline mode, e.g. via an environment variable pointing at a checkout) so the installation path can be exercised without network access.

R11: `README.md`'s installation section starts with exactly the command `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh` as its first installation command, and no `pip install`, `python3 -m venv`, `pipx` or `--user` appears before it or as an alternative main path.

R12: `README.md` retains the Python 3 requirement, the requirement that the `forgel` engine is on PATH including how to point at a custom engine path, exactly one update line (same command with a new tag), and exactly one uninstall line.
R13: `README.md` mentions Windows in a single short line outside the main path, using `pip install --user`, explicitly marked as not the main installation method.
R14: A test guards R11 by parsing `README.md` for ordering, so a later regression fails the suite.

R15: A test runs the real `install.sh` offline against a local source tree into a temporary directory and asserts that the `forgel-code` launcher exists, that `forgel-code --version` prints the installed version with exit code 0, and that a second run exits 0 without breaking the first installation.
R16: A test asserts that with the opt-out variable set no profile file is created or modified and nothing is written outside the temporary target directory.
R17: No file under `forgel_code/` is modified.
acceptance: A1: `README.md` contains the installer line as the first installation command, and its installation section contains no `pipx`, `python3 -m venv` or `pip install` instruction on the main path.
A2: Running `install.sh` in a clean temporary HOME installs the client, prints the installed version and exits with code 0.
A3: After installation, `forgel-code --version` prints the version and exits with code 0.
A4: Running `install.sh` twice in a row exits with code 0 both times and leaves exactly one PATH block in the shell profile.
A5: With the opt-out environment variable set, no profile file is created or modified and the script prints an `export PATH=...` line.
A6: `install.sh --uninstall` removes the installation directory, the launcher and the PATH block it added.
A7: The full test suite passes, including the new README guard and the offline installation tests.
A8: No file under `forgel_code/` is modified.
constraints: Public artifacts are in English (D-025); the chat reply may be Russian.
The client is a thin UI over the engine's parameterized commands (D-002); installation changes must not add model access, project file reads or checks to the client.
The installer must not require network access at run time beyond fetching the script itself, and must work when the source tree is local (used by tests).
Do not weaken or delete existing tests to make the suite pass.
Keep the existing built-in build backend usable; no new third-party runtime dependency.
assumptions: The `code` repository is the target: its README carries the current pip/pipx installation instructions, `pyproject.toml` declares the `forgel-code` entry point, and the package lives under `forgel_code/`.
Default installation directory is `~/.local/share/forgel-code`, overridable by an environment variable; the executable goes to `~/.local/bin`, the conventional per-user bin directory.
The profile file is chosen per shell (`~/.profile` by default, `.bashrc`/`.zshrc` when detectable); the added block is delimited by a comment marker naming Forgel Code.
The opt-out variable is named `FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT` and the install root override `FORGEL_CODE_HOME`.
Uninstall is an explicit `--uninstall` flag on the same script, as 'one command' through the same entry point.
Offline tests invoke the installer with the local source tree (a source override or `sh install.sh` run from the checkout) and a temporary HOME, so no network is used.
The README example keeps the `v0.1.0` tag, matching the current released version.
Windows fallback remains `pip install --user` as a single line outside the main path.

external_dependencies.name: POSIX shell (`/bin/sh`)
external_dependencies.interface: `install.sh` is executed by `sh`, both directly (`sh install.sh`) and via the documented `curl ... | sh` pipeline; the offline installer tests invoke `sh install.sh`.
external_dependencies.evidence: Repository contains an executable `install.sh` at its root written as a POSIX sh script (per the task summary), and the test harness runs it with `sh install.sh`; `/bin/sh` is a locally installed executable available to the test environment.

external_dependencies.name: Python 3 interpreter with `pip` module
external_dependencies.interface: The installer uses `python3` (and, when needed, `python3 -m pip install --target <prefix> .`) to place the client package into the per-user target prefix under `~/.local/share/forgel-code`; the installed `forgel-code` launcher runs the client with `python3 --version`-style invocation. Tests assert `forgel-code --version` exits 0.
external_dependencies.evidence: The offline installation tests are required to run the installer against a local source tree into a temporary directory and then execute `forgel-code --version`, which requires a locally installed `python3` (and the `pip` module used by the installer); both are standard locally installed executables in the project's environment contract.

external_dependencies.name: curl
external_dependencies.interface: Used by the single documented installation command `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh`; it is not executed by the offline test suite (tests stream the local `install.sh` directly).
external_dependencies.evidence: README.md contains exactly one installation command, `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh`, as the first installation step; `curl` is a locally installed executable, and the offline tests substitute the local `install.sh` for the network fetch.

external_dependencies.name: GitHub raw content hosting (`raw.githubusercontent.com`)
external_dependencies.interface: The README's one-line install command targets `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh`. Tests never fetch this URL; the offline tests read the identical `install.sh` from the local repository root, so the network endpoint is emulated by sourcing the vendored script.
external_dependencies.evidence: `install.sh` is present at the repository root (per the task summary and README install command), and the README documents the raw URL as the source of that same script; therefore the raw-hosted artifact can be reproduced deterministically from the local repository check-out.

external_dependencies.name: pytest
external_dependencies.interface: Runs the existing project test suite, including the new README guard test and the real offline installation tests (`sh install.sh` into a temporary HOME, `forgel-code --version`, second run, opt-out, and `--uninstall`).
external_dependencies.evidence: The project's test configuration (pyproject.toml / requirements-dev / tests directory) declares `pytest` as the test runner, and the required README guard and offline installer tests are described as part of the existing pytest suite; `pytest` is a locally installed executable in the project environment.

result.summary:
Продуктовая часть задачи уже реализована и проверена, но финальная приёмочная команда `python -m pytest -q` не может пройти в этом хост-окружении, и изнутри репозитория это не исправить.

Что сделано и зелено (повторно подтверждено в этой попытке):
- `sh -n install.sh` → код 0, права файла 0755, `sh install.sh --help` → код 0 (POSIX `sh`, один файл, годен для `curl … | sh`).
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -q` → `Ran 134 tests in 46.180s … OK` (код 0). Это задокументированный в README способ запуска тестов проекта.
- `/usr/local/bin/pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` с `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` → `134 passed in 46.28s`, код 0.
- `git status`: изменены `README.md`, `tests/test_cli.py`, `tests/test_install.py`, `tests/test_readme_install.py`, новый `install.sh`; под `forgel_code/` изменений нет.

Точная причина падения финальной команды (окружение, не репозиторий):
- Команда `python` указывает на `/Users/okalistratov/.forgel-cli/bin/python3.13`, и для этого интерпретатора pytest не установлен: `python -m pytest -q` → `/Users/okalistratov/.forgel-cli/bin/python3.13: No module named pytest`. Проверка `importlib.util.find_spec('pytest')` для этого интерпретатора и для системного `python3.13` даёт `None`; в его site-packages (`~/.forgel-cli/lib/python3.13/site-packages`) pytest отсутствует.
- Единственный установленный pytest — `/usr/local/bin/pytest` для Python 3.8 (`/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages`, pytest 5.4.3). При обычном запуске он падает ещё до сбора тестов при автозагрузке сторонних плагинов: `faker` → `dateutil` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'six'`. С отключённой автозагрузкой плагинов тот же набор даёт 134 passed.
- Обход внутри репозитория потребовал бы подложить модуль `pytest.py` в корень (затенение настоящего pytest и риск попадания в колесо пакета) — это дефект продукта, а не исправление, и правило «не ослаблять и не подменять тесты» его запрещает. Установка пакета и запись вне репозитория мне запрещены.

Требуемое решение (одно из):
1) Установить pytest для интерпретатора, который резолвится как `python` (3.13): `python -m pip install pytest`; тогда `python -m pytest -q` выполнит существующий набор без изменений в репозитории.
2) Либо запускать приёмку интерпретатором, у которого pytest уже есть, с отключённой автозагрузкой плагинов: `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 /usr/local/bin/pytest -q` (уже проверено: 134 passed).
3) Либо зафиксировать в контракте окружения, что тесты проекта запускаются стандартной библиотекой: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -q` (уже проверено: 134 OK) — репозиторий не объявляет pytest зависимостью (в `pyproject.toml` нет тестовых зависимостей), и все тесты написаны на `unittest`.

До выполнения одного из этих пунктов честно подтвердить `python -m pytest -q` с кодом 0 невозможно; код установщика, README и тестов при этом корректен и полностью зелёный.

env['PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD'] = '1'
